custom_logic_notes: Triangular arbitrage EA monitors three currency pairs forming a triangle (e.g. EURUSD, USDJPY, EURJPY). It computes a synthetic cross rate from two legs and compares it to the actual market rate of the third leg. When the discrepancy exceeds transaction costs (spreads + commissions on all three trades), it simultaneously opens three market orders: two in one direction and one in the opposite direction to capture the mispricing. All three positions must be opened atomically; partial fills create directional risk. The EA likely includes configurable symbol chain inputs (3 pairs), minimum profit threshold in pips/points, lot synchronization logic, and commission/spread deduction. Exit occurs when the arbitrage window closes (prices converge). This strategy is latency-sensitive and typically only profitable with low-spread ECN accounts and co-located VPS. Backtesting is unreliable because triangular arbitrage opportunities are transient and depend on tick-level simultaneous multi-symbol pricing.
python_conversion_notes: Not recommended for Python backtesting conversion. Triangular arbitrage requires: (1) synchronized tick-level data for 3 symbols simultaneously, (2) realistic spread/commission modeling for all 3 legs, (3) execution latency simulation - even 50ms delay eliminates most opportunities, (4) atomic multi-symbol order execution which most backtesting frameworks cannot model. If attempted, use a tick-data backtester with multi-symbol support (e.g. custom vectorbt or backtrader setup with aligned tick feeds). The core logic (synthetic price calculation and discrepancy detection) is straightforward to code, but realistic fill simulation across 3 simultaneous orders is the primary blocker. The EA is fundamentally a live-execution tool, not a backtestable strategy.
